The association is modest and both are MSS conventional adenocarcinomas, so the call is weak-to-moderate. features: A: exophytic villous/papillary architecture with adenoma-like fronds on overview; B: dense cribriform glands with prominent luminal dirty necrosis; B: solid infiltrative conventional growth with desmoplastic stroma; A: tall columnar eosinophilic cells, low-grade villiform epithelium, inflamed stroma

Villous/adenoma-associated growth tends to go with KRAS mutation, while classic cribriform glands with dirty necrosis tend to go with wild-type tumours, so I lean toward A. These associations are weak, and A's fields are partly surface or edge tissue, so the call is only modestly above chance. Slide B shows section folds (the dark lines), which I ignored.

features: A: exophytic villous/papillary fronds with serrated (sawtooth) gland contours; A: retained goblet cells and intracytoplasmic mucin throughout tumour epithelium; B: conventional infiltrative cribriform/solid adenocarcinoma with luminal dirty necrosis; B: desmoplastic stroma with small infiltrating glands, transmural growth into fat
rationale: Slide A is an exophytic, frond-forming tumour with tall columnar epithelium, serrated gland contours, many goblet cells and mucin, and low-to-intermediate nuclear atypia, resembling a villous/serrated phenotype. The sampled A fields are largely superficial (surface fronds) and may not show the invasive front, which limits the comparison. Both slides have folds or artefacts (fold band in A field 2, knife lines in B), which I did not use for the call. The signal is moderate at best.

Stain tone differs (A pink-magenta, B blue-purple), and I gave that no weight. These associations are weak at population level, so this is a modest lean towards B, not a confident call.

features: A: abundant goblet-cell/intracytoplasmic mucin differentiation in tumour glands; B: non-mucinous, goblet-poor; B: luminal dirty (eosinophilic/karyorrhectic) necrosis in several fields; A: largely absent; A: villous/polypoid, adenoma-like tall columnar architecture with mildly serrated luminal borders; B: classic tubular/cribriform adenocarcinoma with pseudostratified cigar-shaped nuclei

The evidence is weak and I judge the call only modestly better than chance.

features: intracytoplasmic goblet-type mucin vacuoles in tumour glands of A, nearly absent in B; focal eosinophilic cytoplasm with serrated/tufted luminal contour in A; B shows conventional tall columnar pseudostratified cigar-shaped nuclei with minimal mucin; more inflamed, desmoplastic stroma in A

The difference is modest and these features overlap widely between genotypes, so the call is weak. Stain tone differs (A pinker/magenta, B bluer/paler), and I did not use it.

features: Slide A shows abundant goblet-cell/intracellular mucin and mucin-containing lumens; slide B epithelium is essentially non-mucinous; Slide A has an exophytic villous/tubulovillous, adenoma-like architecture with cystically dilated mucin glands; Slide B has pencillate, stratified nuclei in non-mucinous villiform glands with loose desmoplastic stroma (conventional NOS pattern)

Slide B is a conventional non-mucinous adenocarcinoma with pencillate nuclei and desmoplastic stroma. Mucinous differentiation and villous-adenoma-like residual growth lean toward KRAS mutation, so I favour A. The separation is modest. Stain tone differs (A is pink-magenta, B is blue-violet), but that difference carries no weight in the call.

features: extensive extracellular mucin pools in slide B (mucinous component on overview and fields); slide A exophytic villous/papillary low-grade growth without mucin; slide B infiltrative desmoplastic glands with dirty necrosis and budding (WT-leaning feature, partly offsets)
rationale: Slide A is an exophytic, villous/papillary, largely superficial adenocarcinoma with pseudostratified columnar epithelium, fibrovascular cores and no extracellular mucin; it has coverslip air artefact and congestion. Mucinous differentiation is the KRAS-associated feature I weight most, so I lean B. Villous architecture in A is also somewhat KRAS-associated, and B's dirty necrosis is a classic conventional pattern, so the signal conflicts and the call is weak. Slide B field 3 was not viewed; the call rests on the other 9 fields and both overviews.

features: extensive extracellular mucin pools in slide B overview (substantial mucinous component); intraluminal mucin in B glands; villous/exophytic papillary architecture in A (counterweight favouring A); dirty necrosis in B glands (counterweight favouring A)

I gave the most weight to B's mucinous component, which leans toward KRAS. A's villous exophytic growth points the other way, and so does B's dirty necrosis, so the evidence conflicts. A's darker, redder staining carries no weight. The call is weak and only slightly better than chance.

features: extracellular mucin pools / mucinous component in B (fields 2,3,5 and overview mucin lakes); A: exophytic villous/villiform low-to-intermediate grade tumour with pseudostratified cigar-shaped nuclei (also a KRAS-compatible pattern); B: higher-grade pleomorphic vesicular nuclei with intraluminal dirty necrosis, deep invasion
rationale: Slide A is a large exophytic, villiform adenocarcinoma with tall columnar cells, pseudostratified elongated nuclei, delicate congested fibrovascular cores and little desmoplasia; it is mostly superficial on the overview. Slide B is a deeply invasive, higher-grade tumour with pleomorphic vesicular nuclei, intraluminal dirty necrosis, desmoplastic stroma and a substantial extracellular mucinous component (mucin lakes visible on the overview and in three fields). Both slides carry features that can go with KRAS mutation: the villous exophytic growth in A and the mucinous differentiation in B. I weighted the mucinous component slightly more and called B. The dirty necrosis in B argues the other way, so the signal is weak and conflicting, and the probability stays close to 0.5. Stain tone differs (A is darker and more saturated), but I did not use this.

features: slide B eosinophilic cytoplasm with pale mucoid/fibrinous luminal material in glands; slide A classic tall-columnar stratified villoglandular pattern with abundant dirty luminal necrosis; slide B more cribriform/solid sheets with focal serrated-like eosinophilic change

Slide B comes from four small, thick fragments with heavy edge artefact and eosin-dense crush. Its tumour has more eosinophilic cytoplasm, cribriform-to-solid sheets and lumens holding pale mucoid/fibrinous material, with less classic dirty necrosis. I weighted that mucoid, eosinophilic phenotype slightly towards KRAS-mutant. The difference is subtle, and B's poor section quality limits how well it can be assessed, so this is a weak lean only.

features: No histologic feature judged independently discriminating; Slide A: conventional crowded tubular/cribriform adenocarcinoma with luminal necrosis; Slide B: eosinophilic cytoplasm, scattered intracytoplasmic vacuoles, frozen-type fragmented section limiting assessment
rationale: Slide A shows conventional moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma: crowded, pseudostratified tubular and cribriform glands with intraluminal necrosis. An earlier version of this call leaned toward B based on mucinous/serrated versus dirty-necrosis features, but that direction matched a prior-study finding surfaced in auto-recalled project memory, so it was not an independent blinded judgement and has been withdrawn. features: intracytoplasmic mucin vacuoles / goblet-like mucin droplets scattered in B epithelium, essentially absent in A; abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm in B (partly confounded by redder stain); A shows conventional villiform/papillary tall-columnar stratified pattern with dirty necrosis (also seen in B), a feature not clearly separating
rationale: Slide A is a conventional, moderately differentiated villiform/papillary-tubular adenocarcinoma: tall stratified columnar cells with pencillate nuclei, cribriform lumens and luminal dirty necrosis. On the overview it invades through muscularis propria into pericolic fat. Slide B is stained much redder, and the tissue is small fragments with blurry edges. Its tumour has eosinophilic cytoplasm and scattered intracytoplasmic mucin vacuoles, with focal clear/mucinous change next to cribriform glands and dirty necrosis. I lean slightly toward B because of the focal mucin production and eosinophilic, serrated-like cytoplasm. But part of B's eosinophilia is stain colour, and A's villous architecture can also fit KRAS. The signal is weak, so the probability stays close to 0.5.

features: B: villous/papillary exophytic fronds with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and lower nuclear:cytoplasmic ratio; A: conventional crowded pseudostratified cigar-shaped nuclei with luminal dirty necrosis; B: large vesicular nuclei with prominent nucleoli, less stratification; occasional goblet-like vacuoles; A overview: infiltrative glandular tumour into muscularis propria with desmoplastic stroma; B overview: bulky exophytic/villous mass

Villous or serrated-like features with abundant cytoplasm and little classic dirty necrosis fit somewhat better with KRAS-mutant tumours, so I favour B. Neither slide has a mucinous component, and the differences are modest, so this is a weak call. Several B fields are surface or fragmented tissue, and A and B differ slightly in stain tone; I did not use tone.

features: B: villous/exophytic fronds lined by tall cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and vesicular nuclei with prominent nucleoli (serrated/villous-like); A: conventional tubular/elongated gland-forming adenocarcinoma with dark, crowded, pseudostratified cigar-shaped nuclei and desmoplastic stroma; Both show luminal dirty necrosis (B overview has extensive pink necrotic areas), so necrosis does not separate them
rationale: Slide A is a classic intestinal-type gland-forming adenocarcinoma: elongated tubular glands with crowded hyperchromatic pseudostratified nuclei, desmoplastic stroma, invasion into muscularis propria on the overview, and focal dirty necrosis. Slide B is a bulky exophytic tumour with villous fronds lined by larger cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and vesicular nuclei with nucleoli, plus inflamed stroma. These features are more serrated- or villous-like. I lean toward B being KRAS-mutant because of that eosinophilic villous/serrated-like phenotype. Neither slide is mucinous, both have necrosis, and the difference is subtle, so this is a weak call. Several of slide A's fields are half empty at tissue edges, which carries no KRAS information.

features: B: abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm with villous/papillary fronds (partly serrated-like) vs A: crowded tubular glands with pencillate stratified nuclei (conventional pattern); B: larger vesicular nuclei with prominent nucleoli; B: extensive intraluminal dirty necrosis on overview (argues the other way, so weakens the call)

Slide B shows tall cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, villous/papillary fronds and larger vesicular nuclei with nucleoli, and extensive luminal dirty necrosis is visible on the overview. I lean toward B as KRAS-mutant because of the eosinophilic-cytoplasm, villous/serrated-leaning phenotype. B's prominent dirty necrosis is a classic conventional feature, though, so the call is weak. No mucinous component is seen in either slide.

features: A: exophytic/polypoid tumour with villoglandular, tall-columnar fronds (field 4) suggesting adenoma-derived growth; A: focal small infiltrating glands in desmoplastic stroma with intraluminal vacuolated/mucin-like contents; B: conventional elongated pseudostratified glands with dirty necrosis and solid/cribriform nests, no villous component
rationale: Both tumours are moderately differentiated conventional adenocarcinomas with tall columnar pseudostratified epithelium and intraluminal necrotic debris, so most features overlap. Slide A has a more exophytic, polypoid overview with villoglandular fronds and some intraluminal vacuolated contents, which I weight slightly toward a KRAS-mutant, adenoma-derived phenotype. Slide B shows classic elongated glands with dirty necrosis and solid/cribriform nests without a villous component. Quality differences (colour gradients and blur in A, ink overlay, crush and fragmentation in B) were not used. The evidence is weak and the call is only slightly better than chance.

features: A: exophytic villous/papillary architecture on overview and fields 1/4; A: frequent intracytoplasmic vacuoles / focal mucinous-type change (fields 2,5); B: conventional glands with luminal dirty necrosis and solid areas; B: large vesicular nuclei, eosinophilic cytoplasm, inflamed stroma
rationale: Slide A is an exophytic polypoid tumour with villous/papillary fronds, crowded elongated pseudostratified nuclei and frequent cytoplasmic vacuoles with focal mucinous-type change. Slide B shows conventional cribriform/tubular adenocarcinoma with prominent luminal dirty necrosis, solid areas, large vesicular nuclei and a congested, inflamed stroma. The villous/mucinous tendency in A and the dirty-necrosis pattern in B tilt me toward A as the KRAS-mutant tumour. The difference is modest and overlaps heavily with ordinary CRC heterogeneity, so the call is weak. Stain differences (A bluer with uneven tone; B has a marker-ink artefact over field 3) were ignored.

features: A: exophytic/villous-appearing polypoid tumour with residual adenomatous-looking surface on overview; A: more intracytoplasmic mucin vacuoles/clear droplets in glands (fields 3-4); B: more solid/cribriform nests with vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli (higher nuclear grade); both: dirty luminal necrosis and conventional gland formation — largely similar

Slide A shows a polypoid/exophytic growth with what looks like adjacent adenomatous/villous surface and more intracytoplasmic mucin vacuoles, features I weakly associate with KRAS-mutant tumours. Slide B is more solid with vesicular, nucleolated nuclei. Stain differences (A bluish cast; B green marker ink in field 1 and fragmented tissue in fields 2, 3 and 5) were ignored. The call is weak and only slightly above chance.

features: A: villiform/papillary fronds with tall columnar, eosinophilic cytoplasm and focal serrated-like tufting; B: crowded cribriform glands with abundant intraluminal dirty necrosis (classic CRC pattern); B: denser peritumoral inflammation, more hyperchromatic stratified nuclei
rationale: Slide A shows a villiform/papillary, more open glandular pattern with tall eosinophilic columnar cells and focal serrated-like tufting, with less dirty necrosis. Slide B shows classic crowded cribriform adenocarcinoma with extensive dirty necrosis and hyperchromatic stratified nuclei, typical of a conventional (often wild-type) colorectal phenotype. Neither slide is mucinous. The serrated/villous features in A lean it toward KRAS-mutant, but the signal is weak and overlaps heavily, so confidence is modest. Slide B has green marker ink over parts of the fields and a darker stain; these were not used in the call.

features: B overview: large exophytic polypoid tumour with villous surface (possible residual villous precursor); B fields: crowded back-to-back tubular/cribriform glands with occasional goblet-like vacuoles; A fields: open villiform fronds with eosinophilic cytoplasm and luminal dirty necrosis; deeply invasive into fat on overview
rationale: Both tumours are conventional, moderately differentiated, non-mucinous adenocarcinomas with tall pseudostratified columnar epithelium. Neither shows meaningful extracellular mucin, so the clearest KRAS-associated feature is absent from both. Slide A has open villiform fronds, eosinophilic cytoplasm, dirty necrosis and deep infiltration into pericolic fat. Slide B is a large exophytic polypoid mass with a villous surface and densely crowded tubular glands. The slight lean toward B rests only on the polypoid, villous-precursor-like architecture, a weak and nonspecific cue, so the call is close to chance. Marker-ink tinting (A field 5; B fields 4 and 5) and blur (A field 4) were treated as artefacts with no KRAS information.

features: slide A: tall columnar cells with more eosinophilic cytoplasm in villiform/papillary fronds, focally serrated-looking; slide B: crowded glands with dense basophilic nuclei and large luminal dirty necrosis (field 4); slide B: large exophytic polypoid mass with surface villous fronds; slide A: deeply infiltrative growth reaching fat, with a lymph node in the section; neither slide has a mucinous component
rationale: Both tumours are conventional, moderately differentiated, non-mucinous adenocarcinomas with luminal necrosis, so neither shows a strong distinguishing feature. In slide A the villiform/papillary epithelium has more eosinophilic cytoplasm and a few serrated-looking contours. Slide B is more crowded and basophilic, with prominent dirty necrosis, which leans slightly towards the wild-type pattern. The difference is subtle and could easily come from sampling, so I set the probability only a little above chance. Green marker ink overlies several slide B fields and lowers its quality. Ink and stain tone did not inform the call.

features: intracytoplasmic mucin vacuoles and goblet-cell-rich villous component in B; cribriform/solid comedo-type pattern with dirty necrosis in B (against KRAS, offsets); eosinophilic cytoplasm with focal serrated-like tufting in A (offsets)
rationale: Slide A shows conventional moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with tall pseudostratified glands, luminal dirty necrosis, eosinophilic cytoplasm and focal tufting; two of its five fields sample eroded surface or near-normal mucosa. Slide B is a more solid/cribriform tumour with luminal necrosis, but with abundant intracytoplasmic mucin vacuoles and a goblet-cell-rich villous component. I gave the mucinous differentiation in B slight weight toward KRAS. B's comedo-type cribriform pattern and A's serrated-like eosinophilic features point the other way. The evidence is conflicting and weak, so the call is close to a coin flip.

features: B: abundant intracytoplasmic and intraluminal mucin vacuoles / partial mucinous (goblet-like) differentiation in multiple fields; A: classic tall-columnar gland-forming adenocarcinoma with prominent luminal dirty necrosis; A: villous/papillary surface fronds; B: more cribriform/solid nests with mucin
rationale: Slide A is a typical moderately differentiated gland-forming adenocarcinoma: tall pseudostratified columnar cells, lumens full of dirty necrosis, and villous surface fronds. Slide B is cribriform to solid, and in fields 1, 3 and 4 it has frequent intracytoplasmic and intraluminal mucin vacuoles, i.e. partial mucinous differentiation. Mucinous features lean KRAS-mutant in my judgement, and classic dirty-necrosis morphology leans the other way, so I call B. Both slides are moderately differentiated and the difference is modest, so I set a weak probability of 0.36 that A is the KRAS-mutant slide. The stain tone differs slightly (B more purple), and I did not use it.

features: B has an extracellular mucin component (pools dissecting solid/cribriform nests in fields 2-3); A has none; B shows abundant intracytoplasmic mucin vacuoles and goblet-like cells within solid/cribriform sheets; A is conventional tubular/villoglandular adenocarcinoma with tall columnar pseudostratified cigar-shaped nuclei and luminal dirty debris; B nuclei are vesicular with prominent nucleoli, in cribriform-solid architecture
rationale: Slide A is a conventional gland-forming adenocarcinoma: tall columnar cells, elongated pseudostratified nuclei, intraluminal necrotic debris, desmoplastic stroma. Its overview shows no mucin lakes. Two of A's five fields (3 and 4) are mostly normal or inflamed mucosa, which limits sampling. Slide B is a cribriform-to-solid tumour with a clear mucinous component: extracellular mucin pools dissect the nests, and there are many intracytoplasmic mucin vacuoles. I weighted B's mucinous differentiation as the main feature and read it as a modest lean toward KRAS mutation. The two tumours differ clearly in morphology, but these features overlap heavily between genotypes, so the call is weak (p_A = 0.38).
